key_insight: LATHE turns crystal editing into a differentiable, hypothesis-driven optimization problem, enabling fine-grained control of seven crystallographic properties from natural language constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical closed-loop workflow for inverse materials design by linking LLM-based hypothesis generation with physically grounded structural editing and evaluation.
method: Expresses bond, angle, dihedral, coordination, lattice, volume, and space-group constraints as differentiable objectives.
Uses gradient-based geometric editing to modify an input crystal structure directly, rather than generating one de novo.
Wraps the toolkit in an MCP server and multi-agent loop that converts natural-language hypotheses into executable design actions.
evidence_signal: Across single-property benchmarks, LATHE achieves near-perfect satisfaction on all seven property types while keeping structures close to local energy minima; in band-gap design, it reaches the target in 9/10 runs with about 13 hypothesis-evaluation cycles.
watch_item: Performance depends on well-posed differentiable objectives and a reliable editing loop, so harder symmetry/chemistry cases may still require careful human oversight and validation.
paper_title: LATHE: LAnguage-driven Toolkit for Hypothesis-based crystal Editing
